item.title: EDDIE MARSAN - Actor
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 211 Eddie Marsan - ActorIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with actor Eddie Marsan (NO ORDINARY HEIST, BACK TO BLACK, RAY DONOVAN). During our conversation, we discuss Eddie's youth in East London, being discovered by casting in a club at 18, his disciplined approach to his craft, working with a range of directors including Mike Leigh (Season 1, Episode 76), Edgar Wright (Season 2, Episode 169), and Steven Spielberg, playing a countless number of supporting roles, and the shortcomings of filmmakers who fail to give working and lower class characters volition, autonomy, and humanity. Eddie also reflects on acting as "evil" characters, and we discuss the qualities of several of them from throughout his career. Towards the end of the episode, we ask Eddie how younger generations of actors are different compared to the ones who came before, and he encourages young actors to not wait for the system to change and create space for the roles they want to play. Plus, Eddie reveals the type of character he'd love to play but has yet to.This episode is sponsored by Aputure

item.title: When an Actor’s Career Fell Apart – Wesley Snipes
item.author: FilmStack
item.content:encoded:
By the late 90s, Wesley Snipes was everywhere.
He broke through with New Jack City, proved he could carry a comedy with White Men Can’t Jump, became an action star with Passenger 57 and Demolition Man, and still found time for films like To Wong Foo and One Night Stand, where he won Best Actor at the Venice Film Festival.
But in 1998, he became Blade.
Blade became the defining role of Snipes’ career. But as Blade got bigger, the rest of his career started slowing down.
Within a few years, the major studio roles were disappearing, stories about his on-set antics were spreading, and legal trouble was about to take him away for years.
This is the story of when an actor disappeared from Hollywood, and how he had to skate uphill to find his way back. This is Wesley Snipes.

item.title: The Decade Hollywood Stopped Saying No
item.author: FilmStack
item.content:encoded:
When Hollywood felt the pressure, they panicked. And what did they do? They gave a generation of directors more control than ever before. That decision sent shockwaves through the film industry and resulted in one of the biggest transformative periods in Hollywood. This was the 1970s and we are still living with the effects from this time period.
Some of the biggest directors ever shined during this time. Steven Spielberg, George Lucas, Francis Ford Coppola, Robert Altman, Martin Scorsese, and more. These directors evolved the film industry more than any others. From Jaws to Star Wars to Apocalypse Now to The Exorcist, this video covers the 1970s like no other video.
This is a story of when Hollywood lost it's way, then lost control, then took that control back, all because of the same reasons.

item.title: RON HOWARD - Director
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 210 Ron Howard - DirectorIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with director Ron Howard (AVEDON, APOLLO 13, A BEAUTIFUL MIND). Ron has worked professionally in film and television since the age of 4, and he reflects on his life and career throughout the episode, from chewing fake glass with Yul Brenner as a child actor to directing a wide variety of features and documentaries for almost 50 years. A graduate of the Roger Corman movie factory, Ron reveals what he learned about leadership and collaboration while directing GRAND THEFT AUTO, his directorial debut, under Roger's guidance, and we discuss whether any modern equivalent exists for filmmakers today as a proving ground. Ron also shares how he pushed himself early on to always be creating, and we discuss the creation of several of his films and what he aims for in every movie he makes. We later ask what draws him to a potential project, and we discuss his foray into directing documentaries and how it differs from shooting fiction. We worked with Ron on A BEAUTIFUL MIND, and we had a wonderful time catching up with him.This episode is sponsored by Aputure ⁠

item.content:encoded: Hey Star Trek! Happy Birthday! - Krebs Gorlon. In this video, two of the ugliest men on Earth sit down to discuss a TV show that is now 60 years old! What more could you possibly want from a YouTube? But in all seriousness Rich and Mark finally go in depth into the very first season of Star Trek! They don’t really have a top 5 episodes, because (according to them) they like all the episodes in some way, kind of how you like something about all of your ugly children. They both pick five or so episodes to discuss or highlight or whatever. Rach and Mooboo love to talk about Star Trek so they doed. They make the time to sit down and talk for nearly three hours. Mark peed in his pants and the dumb one pooped in his diaper. The dumb one is the guy wearing the Scottish hat and the fat, ugly one is the guy that “edits” these videos. I mean, if I were to look up the definition of “editing” I don’t think It would read: “Leaves everything in” but hey, what else are these guys gonna do with little time they have left? They’re literally weeks away from the grave talking about how a 60 year old show was a good show. My god, is this what they are choosing to do with their remaining days??!? Young people today don’t even watch TV or Movies! They don’t have the patience. They watch hip-flips on their switch kicks and play Rubblox on their hyperinterlinked cerebrum-chips. Getting someone under 45 to watch an episode of Star Trek is like getting an old in the grocery store to move to one side of the aisle while walking in slow motion searching for salve. Life has become a nightmare from which I can’t escape. An endless series of holidays and birthdays that all culminate in an endless series of hospital visits and funerals. In the middle of all that we eat, we sleep, and we watch TV. So in this 2 hour long video about Star Trek Mark and Ronaldo first discuss a few off topic topics. Mainly the current state of Star Trek. We are in the middle of the streaming of season 4 of Strange New Worlds (With a short season 5 yet to come) and one more season of Starfleet Academy (Viewership predicted to be less than 100) After that who can truly say what is next for a once beloved franchise that looks like a beaten up grandma. I guess them two guys are writing a movie where Star Trek is going to be some kind of spy action thriller and they are bringing back Khan. Oh boy! Can't wait for that. I hate this world and I hate the people that are in charge of entertainment today. A bunch of fart clowns I say it. FART CLOWNS. The dumbest people on earth are in charge. They say you can never go home again. But with old TV shows you can. You can put on an old show or movie and watch it and say, "Ah, this is nice. This doesn't hurt me so deeply" As Mark and Raunch's bodies begin to rot from the inside and their vision begins to blur. As their farts begin to slip out as they lose anal elasticity, they can always sit back and watch and talk about old Star Trek. These two men are made of ash, moments before a strong wind blows through. So enjoy things while they last because you never know when a dimwit is gonna roll into town with a circus of low talent scum TV writers and 58 producers and ruin your whole life.

The Take is now on Patreon: www.patreon.com/kermodeandmayo Become a Vanguardista or an Ultra Vanguardista to get video episodes of Take Two every week, plus member-only chat rooms, polls and submissions to influence the show, behind-the-scenes photos and videos, the monthly Redactor’s Roundup newsletter, and access to a new fortnightly LIVE show - a raucous, unfiltered lunchtime special with the Good Doctors, new features, and live chat so you can heckle, vote, and have your questions read out in real time.
This week’s special guest is Hollywood stalwart Bill Pullman, who across the decades has starred in Independence Day, Spaceballs, David Lynch’s Lost Highway, Sleepless in Seattle and many more. This time we see him in Everybody Digs Bill Evans, where he plays the father of the titular jazz legend. He chats to Simon about father-son stories, jazz, and how working in black and white changes his acting.
Mark will review Everybody Digs Bill Evans next week, and in the meantime we’ve got a packed show with four big screen releases up for the Good Doctors’ judgement. We’ve got Late Fame, a New York set indie about an aging former poet (Willem Dafoe), who is surprised to find his work reappraised by a group of young bohemians. Then there’s Leviticus, an Australian conversion therapy horror from the producers of The Babadook and Talk To Me, and Supernature, a love letter to nature documentary shot entirely on Super 8. And finally, following our interview with director Michael Sarnoski last week, the wait is over for Mark’s verdict on The Death of Robin Hood.
All that plus an especially groan-inducing Laughter Lift, and all your top correspondence, including some great What’s On bulletins this week.

item.title: ROBIN SWICORD - Writer / Director
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 209 Robin Swicord - Writer / DirectorIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with writer and director Robin Swicord (WAKEFIELD, WHEN THEY SEE US, PRACTICAL MAGIC). Throughout the episode, Robin is frank about her experience working in the film industry as a woman, and we discuss how she's seen the culture and behaviour within the industry change over the years. Robin wrote the script for the 1994 adaptation of LITTLE WOMEN, and she shares what it took for the studio to finally greenlight the film after 12 years of development. She also reflects on the long development process of BENJAMIN BUTTON, and she reveals what her initial vision for the story was. After years as a writer, Robin was able to direct her first feature, THE JANE AUSTEN BOOK CLUB, and she shares how she cast the film on short notice and how she prepped for it as a first-time director. We later discuss how she shot her second film as a director, WAKEFIELD, in just 18 days, and she reflects on what she brought from her experiences on her first film to the second one.This episode is sponsored by Aputure ⁠
